newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma again bars access to road near Suu Kyi home.
newsitem.headline: Burma again bars access to road near Suu Kyi home.

text.p: Burmese military authorities on Saturday again blocked public access to democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi's residence, apparently to stop weekend public gatherings outside her house, witnesses said.
Police mounted checkpoints at Rangoon's University Avenue and turned away traffic from the road on which Suu Kyi's house is located.
Witnesses said the checkpoints were set up just after midnight on Saturday. They were manned by traffic police who were backed by security police.

Police had earlier barred access to Suu Kyi's house on September 26, to stop a planned September 27-29 congress of her National League for Democracy Party (NLD). They removed the checkpoints last Tuesday.
The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) also detained 573 NLD members and supporters in a crackdown at that time to thwart the congress. All were later released in stages.
No comment was available from police or the SLORC on how long the access to Suu Kyi's home would be blocked, but residents in the area believed the blockade would last until Monday.

Attempts to reach Suu Kyi by telephone for her comments were unsuccessful. The Nobel laureate had told reporters on Tuesday after the barriers were removed that she was ready to hold her weekend public meetings again if there was access to University Avenue.

The weekend public gatherings in the past have attracted several thousands to hear her attack the SLORC and demand greater democracy in Burma from the gates of her lakeside home. The SLORC has said such meetings are illegal.
Burma's action against Suu Kyi and NLD supporters last month was condemned by the United States, Britain and international human rights groups.

U.S. President Bill Clinton responded to the Burmese action by barring entry to the United States of Burmese military government officials and members of their family. Rangoon reacted by restricting visas to certain categories of U.S. citizens.
